tasks.instruction: Read the text below. Decide if each sentence (1.1-1.4) is True (T), False (F), or if the information is Not In the text (NI).
tasks.text:
THE LONGEST DAY

Every June our school organises a sponsored walk along the coast path, and this year I finally signed up. My friend Kasia had done it twice before and warned me that the last five kilometres were the worst, but I did not really believe her.

We set off at seven in the morning from the harbour, forty-two of us in bright yellow T-shirts. The first hour felt like a holiday. The sea was flat and grey, gulls followed us hoping for sandwiches, and Mr Nowak, our geography teacher, kept stopping to point out rock formations that nobody was interested in.

By eleven the sun was out and the path had turned uphill. Somebody's water bottle had leaked into their bag, and two people had already changed their socks. Kasia walked beside me and said nothing at all, which is how I knew she was struggling too.

The last section runs along the cliff top, and there is no shade of any kind. I remember thinking that if I stopped I would never start again, so I did not stop. We reached the lighthouse at twenty past four, which was slower than the school record but faster than last year's group.

Between us we raised enough money to buy new instruments for the school orchestra. I am not in the orchestra and I have no plans to join it, but I have already written my name down for next June. Kasia says I will regret it. She is probably right.

items.statement: The narrator had walked the coast path with the school in an earlier year.
items.explanation: FALSE - the narrator says 'this year I finally signed up'. It was Kasia who had done it twice before.

items.statement: Kasia found the walk easy this time.
items.explanation: FALSE - she 'said nothing at all, which is how I knew she was struggling too'.

items.statement: The money raised will be spent on musical instruments.
items.explanation: TRUE - 'we raised enough money to buy new instruments for the school orchestra'.

items.statement: Mr Nowak is the teacher who organises the walk each year.
items.explanation: NOT IN THE TEXT - the school organises the walk and Mr Nowak is on it, but the text never says who organises it.
